races.title: State House, District 111
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Paul Scott
cands.bio: Republican state representative for North Carolina House District 111 since January 2025. Senior pastor of Big Springs Baptist Church, volunteer firefighter, sheriff's office chaplain and crisis negotiator, former Rutherford County school board member, and former Duke University Health System technology architect.
cands.gaps: We could not find the year Paul Scott moved to North Carolina. We found no documented stances or actions on data centers, development, property taxes, immigration, guns, abortion or school choice, and no bills he sponsored were listed in the pages we could read. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2024 or 2026, and Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him. His campaign site describes his background but does not lay out policy positions.

local.label: Roots 40: He was born and raised in Florida. His campaign site shows him in North Carolina as an adult since his first pastorate in Morrisville, and he has been senior pastor at Big Springs Baptist Church for fifteen years and a Polkville firefighter for fourteen. The exact arrival year is not given.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: He has served in the NC House since 2025 and previously held a seat on the Rutherford County Board of Education. He holds an MBA and worked as a system administrator and then customer support manager at Duke University Health System. He has also been a pastor, firefighter and sheriff's office chaplain.
qual.why: He has prior legislative service and local elected office, plus an MBA and management experience. The office's rubric puts that in the high range, but he is only one term into legislative service and has no law or dedicated budget career.

cands.name: Jerry Blake
cands.bio: Jerry Blake was the Democratic nominee for North Carolina House District 111 in 2026. He advanced without a primary and lost the general election to incumbent Republican Paul Scott. The sources found give no information on his career or offices held.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as recommended by two voter-guide groups (Sway voting groups): Better Future NC (Cam Pruette) and Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy (Tevin Davis).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Jerry Blake was born or raised, when he came to North Carolina, or his career and work history. He has held no office we could confirm. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, and we found no campaign website, interviews or questionnaires. We therefore have no record of his stated positions on data centers, property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or schools, and no record of any controversies.
